description: Η μελέτη αφορά την ανέγερση των νέων διδακτηρίων Γυμνασίου & Γενικού Λυκείου Χώρας της Δ.Ε. Νέστορος του Δήμου Πύλου – Νέστορος. Προβλέπεται η κατασκευή δυο νέων κτιρίων, τα οποία χωροθετούνται στην περίμετρο του οικοπέδου και σε σχήμα Π. Κατά μήκος της οδού Προφήτη Ηλία και στην βόρεια πλευρά του οικοπέδου τοποθετείται η κύρια κτιριακή μονάδα του Γυμνασίου Χώρας. Στην δυτική πλευρά του οικοπέδου και κατά μήκος αυτής, τοποθετείται η κύρια κτιριακή μονάδα του Γενικού Λυκείου Χώρας. Το συνολικό συγκρότημα αποτελείται από ισόγεια εμβαδού δόμησης 1451.31μ2, ορόφους εμβαδού δόμησης 984.31μ2 και υπόγεια εμβαδού επιφάνειας 521.62μ2. Στον πυρήνα των κτιριακών μονάδων διαμορφώνεται ο αύλειος χώρος των σχολείων και τα στέγαστρα τα οποία εξυπηρετούν κάθε μονάδα. Στη Νότια πλευρά του οικοπέδου διαμορφώνονται τα υπαίθρια γήπεδα, ένα γήπεδο καλαθοσφαίρισης και ένα γήπεδο πετοσφαίρισης για κάθε σχολική μονάδα με τις υπαίθριες κερκίδες τους και ανακατασκευάζεται το υφιστάμενο γήπεδο 5x5. Στην αρχική φάση του έργου προβλέπεται η κατεδάφιση των υφιστάμενων κτιρίων, σύμφωνα με τη μελέτη κατεδάφισης.

The Construction Manager will be required to provide the necessary Construction Management services to ensure the successful completion of all Projects under the Program. These services apply to all construction activities associated with the Projects, are divided into two (2) components and include, but are not limited to, the following: Pre-construction Services: General Services, Pre-design, Schematic Design, Design Development, Construction Document, and Construction Procurement. Construction Services: General Services, Cost Control and Accounting, and Post-Construction Services. Additional details are provided in the RFP document. The resulting Contract will include an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) that aims to provide opportunities for businesses owned and lead by Indigenous People. Canada’s free trade agreements pose no impediment to the inclusion of measures for the benefit of Indigenous Peoples and/or businesses in a procurement. Refer to the RFP documents for more details. title: APN - Ramp B East Replacement Project 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Ramp B East Replacement Project 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at 15 Wing Moose Jaw. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES CFB 15 Wing Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, requires the repair and replacement of the existing Ramp B East at the airbase.The Department of National Defence and Defence Construction Canada intends to put in place a contract to provide all labour, materials, and equipment for work including, but not necessarily limited to, the following:    Installation of temporary security fencing and construction barriers  Demolition and removal of existing concrete pavement  Partial removal of existing granular base  Topsoil stripping and stockpiling  Grading and compaction of the existing granular base and placement of new granular base  Construction of new Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavements  Installation of new joint sealant and paint markings  Landscaping, including topsoil, fertilizer, and hydroseeding  It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: CN88327 Title: Ramp B East Replacement Project , 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK Approximate Estimate: $16,000,000 Anticipated Posting: January 2027 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a tenderer will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS) 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a tender for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a tender.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the tenderer will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Wiley Reid Team Leader, Programs Defence Construction Canada 306-513-5681 Wiley.Reid@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the tenderer agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the tenderer for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

description: 1. GENERAL INFORMATION The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Corporate Services and Acquisition Division (CSAD), Facilities Engineering Office � Eastern Region (FEO-WR) is soliciting Standard Form 330 (SF330) packages from qualified Architect-Engineer (A/E) firms. This procurement is being conducted in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 36.2 with The Brooks Act) (40 U.S.C. 1101 et seq). IDIQ Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). Total Capacity: The total shared capacity of the Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) shall not exceed $9.9M to be allocated among successful offerors over the life of the contract. Guaranteed Minimum: A minimum of $2,500 in task order work shall be awarded under the contract. Period of Performance: Five (5) year ordering period. Individual requirements will be executed via Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task orders. 2. SCOPE OF SERVICES The purpose of the contract is to obtain professional multi-discipline architectural, engineering, and construction management services for repair, renovation, alteration, new construction and expansion across DOC/NOAA facilities, with design excellence and adherence to sound design practices, resulting in projects that meet NOAA�s requirements and are delivered in a cost effective and efficient manner. The A-E shall furnish all necessary personnel, equipment, materials, and services to perform individual firm-fixed-price task orders as required. Typical A/E services include the following: project management, master and strategic planning, facility programming, facility condition assessments (FCA), geotechnical and soil investigations, land surveying (topographic, boundary, and utility), cost estimating, value engineering, engineering studies and analyses, architectural and engineering design services (including design-build and traditional design-bid-build), interior design, furniture design and procurement, seismic studies, coastal engineering, environmental assessments and industrial hygiene, historic preservation and archaeological surveys, commissioning/re-commissioning/retro-commissioning, construction management, construction administration, quality assurance, construction inspection services, life-cycle cost analysis, peer reviews, claims consultation, security and acoustical studies, and post-occupancy evaluations. Typical projects include Design and construction support for new facilities as well as the renovation, repair, expansion, and demolition of existing facilities. Services encompass seismic design and structural retrofits; fire-life safety design in accordance with NFPA and applicable codes; comprehensive facility condition assessments and existing condition reporting; and pre-design site investigations, including utility analysis. Scope includes the repair, alteration, improvement, and remodeling of building exteriors, interior spaces, and building systems�such as mechanical, plumbing, electrical, structural, fire protection, roofing, elevator/escalator systems, and specialized seawater systems. Work extends to the preservation and renovation of historic structures, as well as the repair and new construction of coastal and marine infrastructure, including piers, jetties, wharves, and seawalls. Typical facilities include Office buildings, Warehouses and storage buildings, Laboratories and research facilities, Wharf and pier structures/infrastructure, Seawalls and other coastal construction, Communications installations, Weather forecast offices, Data centers, and Communication/data equipment installations/platforms. 3. GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE While the Government reserves the right to utilize the contractor in other U.S. locations on an exception basis, the primary geographic areas are defined as follows: Eastern Region: Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. 4. CONSIDERATION To be considered under this Request for Qualifications, firms must demonstrate the capability of providing the following minimum requirements: 1) Architectural, civil/structural, geotechnical, seismic design engineering, mechanical, electrical, marine, fire-life safety engineering, and LEED design in conformance to each project jurisdiction; 2) Demonstrated capability of key personnel to respond promptly and effectively to unforeseen emergencies within the primary project locations; 5. EVALUATION CRITERIA The Government plans to award up to three (3) separate A-E Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts to comprise one (1) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for professional A-E services from this announcement. Each respondent�s SF 330 submittal package will be evaluated in accordance with RFO 36.202 procedures. The selection criteria, in descending order of importance will be as follows: 1. Specialized Experience/Technical Competence 2. Professional Qualifications 3. Past Performance The Government will select at least three of the most highly qualified firms for interviews. The Government will evaluate offerors based on the following factors, listed in descending order of importance. The Government will conduct a comprehensive assessment of each offeror�s submission and relevant qualifications to determine the most highly-qualified firms. Factor 1: Specialized Experience and Technical Competence Offerors will be evaluated on the relevancy, breadth, and diversity of their specialized experience as detailed in SF 330, Part 1, Sections F, G, and H, specifically considering projects from the past five (5) years in terms of type, size, and complexity. Demonstrated expertise in Design-Build (specifically RFP development), Construction Administration, and commitment to sustainable energy/design (LEED/Green Globes) is critical. Respondents must provide five (5) recent and relevant projects; any project provided in addition to the five will not be considered. Submissions missing any of the following requested information will be assessed a deficiency: Contract/Task Order Number Project Title Location Prime Firm with % of self-performed work Start and Completion dates If the project is not yet complete, identify the current phase/stage of the project. Fully completed projects will carry more weight than projects still in design Description of the project in sufficient detail and clearly document how it is relevant to the scope of this project Factor 2: Professional Qualifications Offerors will be evaluated on the professional qualifications of key personnel from the primary firm and proposed consultants, as evidenced by SF 330, Part 1, Section E. Evaluation will prioritize professional registration; education, training, and relevant experience; tenure with the firm; and specialized certifications (e.g., DBIA, CEP, NEBB/BCA for CxA). Offerors will be evaluated on the firm�s capacity to manage large, multi-disciplined, complex design efforts and execute multiple concurrent task orders across the diverse Eastern Region. The Government will assess the adequacy of in-house disciplines, the strength of established consulting partners, and the quality of proposed plans for staff augmentation and project response. Factor 3: Past Performance Offerors will be evaluated on their past performance history on recent and relevant contracts for A-E services with Government agencies and private industry. title: Solicitation: Residential Reentry Services and Home Confinement Services within Springfield, Illinois. Home Confinement radius within 200 miles of the RRC Faciliy.
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is soliciting proposals to provide Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services, including in-house RRC beds, and Home Confinement (HC) services for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States statutes. The RRC facility shall be located within the Illinois Counties of Adams, Brown, Pike, Scott, Morgan, Cass, Menard, Sangamon, Macoupin, Greene, Montgomery, Christian, Dewitt, Macon, Piatt, Champaign, Moultrie, Coles, Douglas, Ford, Vermillion, and Edgar. Home Confinement services shall be provided within a 200-mile radius of the RRC facility. RRC and Home Confinement services shall be provided in accordance with the BOP Statement of Work entitled �Residential Reentry Center, March 2022� and the terms and conditions of the solicitation. Home Confinement requirements are addressed in Chapter 10, Programs, and other applicable provisions of the Statement of Work. Contract Structure and Requirements The Government anticipates awarding an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with firm-fixed unit prices, consisting of a one-year base period and four one-year option periods. The solicitation also includes a provision for a potential extension of services for up to six months under FAR 52.217-8. RRC services: The base-year guaranteed minimum is 9,490 inmate days, consisting of 8,030 male inmate days and 1,460 female inmate days, equivalent to 26 beds over a 365-day base period. The estimated maximum capacity is 50 beds: 43 male and 7 female. Home Confinement services: The estimated maximum is 25 placements. No guaranteed minimum is established for Home Confinement services. The guaranteed minimum applies only to base-year RRC services. No guaranteed minimum is established for option years or an extension period. Tiered Pricing Offerors shall provide separate pricing for RRC and Home Confinement services using the tiered pricing schedule in Section B of the solicitation. RRC services: Tier 1: Fixed monthly pricing for an average daily population (ADP) of 20 or fewer. Tier 2: Inmate day pricing for an ADP of 21 through 30. Tier 3: Inmate day pricing for an ADP of 31 through 40. Tier 4: Inmate day pricing for an ADP of 41 or more, with an estimated maximum capacity of 50. Home Confinement services: Tier 1: Fixed monthly pricing for an ADP of 10 or fewer. Tier 2: Placement day pricing for an ADP of 11 through 15. Tier 3: Placement day pricing for an ADP of 16 through 20. Tier 4: Placement day pricing for an ADP of 21 or more, with an estimated maximum of 25 placements. The Government intends to award both RRC and Home Confinement services to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. Offerors shall submit prices for all applicable CLINs as required by the solicitation. The Government reserves the right to make award in its best interest in accordance with the solicitation. Solicitation Availability and Proposal Submission RFP 15BRRC27R00000013 is issued November 23, 2026. Proposals must be received no later than December 23, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time. The solicitation and associated attachments are available electronically through SAM.gov. Hard copies will not be provided. Interested parties are responsible for downloading and reviewing the complete solicitation, all attachments, and any amendments, and for monitoring SAM.gov for updates. Proposals shall be submitted electronically in Adobe Acrobat (PDF) format to Brian Navarette, Contracting Officer, at bnavarette@bop.gov, in accordance with Section L.4 of the solicitation. Proposals shall consist of the following separate volumes: Volume I: Technical/Management Proposal Volume II: Business Proposal Volume III: Past Performance Information Offerors shall comply with all submission instructions in Section L.4, including the 20 MB email-size limit, the requirement to email the Contracting Officer six hours before the closing time stating that a proposal submission is forthcoming, and the requirement to request verification of receipt. All responsible sources may submit a proposal, which will be considered by the agency. Questions regarding this solicitation shall be directed to bnavarette@bop.gov. Funds are not presently available for this solicitation. No award will be made until funds are available and confirmed in writing by the Contracting Officer. The Government reserves the right to cancel the solicitation before or after the closing date and will not reimburse proposal preparation or submission costs. The solicitation and any amendments govern the requirements of this acquisition.

title: Commercial Vessel Long-Term Charter & Multiyear Leasing Strategy
description: Request for Information (RFI) Commercial Vessel Long-Term Charter & Multiyear Leasing Strategy Issuing Organization: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO) Requiring Activities: Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO), National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), and other NOAA Line Offices 1. Summary The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is conducting market research to evaluate the commercial maritime industry's ability to provide vessel capacity in support of NOAA missions through long-term charter, lease, and related commercial arrangements. While NMFS survey charters represent the primary use of commercial capacity, this strategy also encompasses specialized oceanographic missions for other NOAA Line Offices. NOAA is particularly interested in understanding whether longer-term Government commitments can expand access to commercially available vessel capacity, reduce charter costs, improve operational availability, and provide industry with sufficient demand certainty to justify modifications, recapitalization, or other investments needed to support scientific missions. NOAA is evaluating the use of its statutory vessel acquisition and multiyear contracting authorities, specifically 33 U.S.C. � 891d, which grants NOAA the authority to execute multi-year vessel contracts of up to seven years. NOAA welcomes industry perspectives on fully crewed time charters, demise (bareboat) leasing, owner-maintained arrangements, and other commercially viable structures. NOAA is not seeking a single vessel capable of performing every mission. NOAA requires access to a geographically distributed portfolio of commercial vessel capabilities. Respondents may address one or more geographic regions, mission areas, global capacity or vessel classes described in this RFI. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes, does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), and does not commit NOAA to issue a solicitation. No entitlement to payment of direct or indirect costs or charges by the Government will arise as a result of the submission of information. All information considered proprietary shall be marked accordingly, and properly identified proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with federal regulations. The Government shall not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for improperly identified proprietary information. The purpose of this announcement is solely to gather information from the marketplace, and any responses received will neither be considered an offer by the responding party nor returned to the responding party. No telephone inquiries will be accepted, and requests for solicitation packages will not be honored at this time since no solicitation has been prepared. 2. Background NOAA conducts fisheries, protected-species, ecosystem, oceanographic, charting, and related scientific operations throughout U.S. coastal, offshore, and remote ocean areas. Historically, NMFS operations account for approximately 95% of NOAA's charter volume. The remaining 5% of charter volume supports other Line Offices, including the National Ocean Service (NOS), National Weather Service (NWS), and Oceanic and Atmospheric Research (OAR). These missions involve buoy placement and recovery, weather sampling equipment deployment, weather tower construction, and Unmanned Maritime Systems (UMS) deployment. NOAA is evaluating whether longer-term commercial arrangements could provide greater capability, lower costs, increased vessel availability, and stronger incentives for private-sector investment compared to individual short-duration or annual task orders. 3. NOAA Commercial Vessel Capability Envelope Vessel needs vary substantially by geography, mission, season, and scientific activity. The capability areas described below are intended to communicate the breadth of NOAA's potential demand and should not be interpreted as requirements for any single vessel. Geographic Operating Areas NOAA is interested in commercial vessel capacity throughout its operating regions, including Alaska and Arctic waters; the Great Lakes; the U.S. West Coast and adjacent offshore waters; the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic and adjacent offshore waters; the Southeast, Gulf of America, and Caribbean; Equatorial Pacific and the Pacific Islands. Fisheries, Living Marine Resources, and Ecosystem Surveys NMFS requires access to commercial vessels capable of supporting living marine resource (LMR) assessments, fisheries science, and essential fish habitat conservation. Depending on the region and mission, required capabilities may include bottom, midwater, and pelagic trawling, scallop dredging, long-lining, trap/pot, hook-and-line, and towed instrumentation. Associated activities include catch handling, CTD profiling, plankton net deployment, hydroacoustics, and eDNA collection. Protected Species, Oceanography, and Small-Boat Operations NOAA conducts marine mammal, sea turtle, seabird, and ecosystem research, which may require vessels capable of supporting visual observation, scientific diving, live-boating, and small-boat deployment. Additional missions include charting and mapping operations to monitor the status and trends of marine ecosystems. Offshore, Deep-Water, and Subsea Operations NOAA requires commercial vessels capable of supporting deep ocean (up to 6,000 m) oceanographic moorings, remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), Unmanned Maritime Systems (UMS) deployment, deep-water optical surveys, and subsea sampling. Such missions may require precision station keeping, dynamic positioning (DP) class capabilities, specialized oceanographic winches, heavy A-frames, high endurance, large deck storage capacity, heavy-lift A-frame/winch, and containerized laboratory installations. 4. Information Requested from Industry NOAA requests that respondents focus on the commercial market, available capacity, and recommended acquisition approaches. A. Vessel Characteristics, Specifications, and Availability For the geographic regions and mission areas your organization could support, please provide the following vessel specifications: General Info: Vessel name, flag, year built, classification society, and IMO number. Dimensions & Tonnage: Length overall (LOA), beam, draft, molded depth, Gross Tonnage (GT), and Net Tonnage (NT). Deck Space: Clear deck area and maximum deck load capacity. Performance: Service speed, maximum speed at specific fuel consumption rates, maximum endurance (operational days without resupply), and seakeeping (weather limits). Special Gear: Crane capacities, dynamic positioning (DP) class, A-frames, and winches. Commercial Details: Vessel location, homeport, availability dates, daily charter rates, mobilization/demobilization costs, fuel terms, and policies regarding sub-chartering or third-party equipment. Scientific & Living Support: Berthing capacity, Wet/Dry Lab sq footage, walk-in sample freezers/refrigerators, potable water generation capacity. Electrical & Clean Power: auxiliary generator capacity, clean power buses/UPS for sensitive electronics, and high-voltage deck power plugs for containerized vans. Communications & IT Infrastructure: Satellite communication capabilities (VSAT, Starlink), real-time bandwidth limits Vessel Certifications: Any endorsements or certifications that the vessel maintains or is capable of attaining (SOLAS, etc) B. Operating Models: Time Charter vs. Demise Charter NOAA is evaluating the operational, legal, and cost trade-offs between Time Charters (Vendor Operated) and Demise/Bareboat Charters (NOAA Operated). Under Demise Charters, NOAA assumes full command of the vessel to achieve 'Public Vessel' status under 46 U.S.C. � 2101, allowing for rights to modify the vessel with specialized scientific equipment. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity Contract (IDIQ) with a five-year ordering period consisting of a three-year base period and two one-year option periods. This acquisition will support continued and improved supply availability for a critical DLA-managed item. This procurement is being conducted as Other than Full and Open Competition. The Government reserves the right to make award on a Best Value basis. While price may be a significant evaluation factor, award may be made to an offeror other than the lowest-priced offeror after consideration of factors including, but not limited to, price, past performance, delivery performance, and other evaluation criteria identified in the solicitation. Item Description: CLIN 0001 NSN: 2930-014332550 Nomenclature: cooler, lubricating oil, engine Approved Source Item Export Control Applies Contractor First Article Test (FAT) Requirement Applies Surge Requirements Apply Contract Requirements: Inspection and Acceptance: Origin FOB: Source Requested Delivery: 90 Days After Receipt of Order (ARO) once FAT approved Technical Data: This project contains source-controlled drawings/specifications. You may access them through the following link: https://tdmt.dla.mil. Drawings are available directly from TDMT by querying for MR014332550 in the Solicitation field. Trade Agreements / Domestic Preference: One or more of the items under this acquisition may be subject to an Agreement on Government Procurement approved and implemented in the United States by the Trade Agreements Act of 1979. title: Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) Launch Services
description: 11/13/2026 1. The on-ramp proposal due date has been changed from 12/10/2026 to 12/23/2026. 2. Appendix A Past Performance Questionaire template has been uploaded to the attachments/links section. ************************************************************** NASA Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) Launch Services 2026 On-Ramp The NASA Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare (VADR) Launch Services Request for Proposal (RFP) was issued on May 27, 2021 and remains open for a period of five years from the effective date through the use of an innovative on-ramp provision found in Section 2.11, Clause 2.11.1. The VADR contract�s ordering period remains valid through five years from date of contract award. Currently, there are 13 eligible providers as part of the Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ). These providers are Arrow Science and Technology, LLC, Astra Space, Inc., Blue Origin, LLC, Firefly Aerospace, Inc., Impulse Space, Inc., L2 Solutions, LLC, Momentus Space, LLC, Northrup Grumman System Corp., Phantom Space Corp., Relativity Space, Inc., Rocket Lab USA, Inc., Space Exploration Technologies, Corp., and United Launch Services, LLC. During the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from launch service providers for new IDIQ contracts. At a minimum, launch services proposed under VADR require the below: 1. Launch site agreements for at least one launch site to be used in support of task orders awarded under this contract. 2. Evidence of at least one of the following: Launch attempt (intentional ignition) of common launch vehicle configuration being proposed including, but not limited to, the outcome of the launch attempt Successful launch reaching an altitude of 100km or greater (can include any launch vehicle in the Offeror�s fleet) Development tests demonstrating at least 50% of the flight thrust at the complete full-scale single engine assembly level for all core stage engines of the common launch vehicle configuration being proposed. 3. If Offeror is proposing to use a launch vehicle provided by another company e.g., broker services, transfer vehicle, agreements will be required for each proposed vehicle. Original RFP link: https://sam.gov/opp/587b4fae322942b292baccda3098ae13/view (copy and paste into browser) The anticipated RFP will be restricted to domestic sources as described below: DOMESTIC SOURCE CRITERIA In addition to the certification regarding United States commercial provider of space transportation services (Public Law 105?303, Title II, Section 201), the Contractor shall continue to comply with domestic source criteria established below and with United States National Space Transportation Policy, dated November 21, 2013. Failure to comply with the criteria may be grounds for �Termination for Cause� in accordance with FAR 52.212?4(m). Participation in this procurement is restricted to prime Contractors from the United States launch vehicle/services industry. �United States industry� means any corporation, partnership, joint venture, association, or other entity which is organized or existing under the laws of the United States or any State, and whose controlling interest is held by United States citizens. �Launch services� means all services required in the performance of this contract, excluding those necessary to produce or manufacture launch vehicles, its components and other equipment and facilities required in the performance of the contract. �Controlling interest� means ownership of an amount of equity in such entity sufficient to direct management or to void transactions entered into by management. Ownership of at least fifty?one (51) percent of the equity creates a rebuttable presumption that such interest is controlling; however, the ultimate determination as to whether the interest is controlling resides with NASA. The Contractor shall provide in the performance of this contract launch vehicles that are domestic end products. The launch vehicle shall be a domestic end product only if the cost of its components, mined, produced or manufactured in the United States exceeds 50 percent of the cost of all its components. The cost of each component includes transportation costs to the place of incorporation into the launch vehicle and any applicable duty (whether or not a duty?free entry certificate is issued). �Components,� as used in this contract clause, means those materials and supplies directly incorporated into the end product. The Contractor shall provide, in the performance of this contract, domestic launch services. Launch services shall be considered to be domestic if the cost for launch services performed by United States industry sources exceeds 50 percent of the cost of the total required launch services. It is requested that any interested party notify NASA of intent to submit a proposal during this on-ramp period as well as a description of the launch vehicle configuration(s) you intend to propose and current flight manifest. If no viable responses are received, NASA will not conduct a 2026 VADR On-Ramp. An ombudsman has been appointed in accordance with NFS 1852.215-84.

title: USS OKANE (DDG-77); 7MRB0604 Standalone
description: The Southwest Regional Maintenance Center (SWRMC) is hereby issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) No. N5523627R0007 for the execution of the Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs for USS OKANE (DDG-77) Rigid Hull Inflatable Boat (RHIB): 7MRB0604. The Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs for USS OKANE (DDG-77) RHIB: 7MRB0604is anticipated to take approximately nine (9) months beginning on January 25, 2027, through October 10, 2027. The repairs shall be performed at a contractors facility within a 50-mile radius of Naval Base San Diego. The acquisition and solicitation-to-award process shall abide by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul, Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) and the Navy Marine Corps Acquisition Regulation Supplement (NMCARS) guidelines. The Government anticipates awarding this effort as a supply contract whereas the supply equates to the procurement of a repaired, mission-ready USS OKANE (DDG-77) RHIB: 7MRB0604 to be returned to service to the Fleet. The scope of work includes all labor, supervision, production, testing and quality assurance necessary to prepare for and accomplish the Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs. Offerors shall be registered in the Solicitation Module in Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) and System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible for award. Offerors shall be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible for award. The RFP will be a Total Small Business Set-Aside and the applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 336611, Ship Building and Repairing (a small business must have 1,300 or less employees). Award will be based on a lowest technically acceptable. Click enclosed link PIEE Solicitation Module Link for N5523627R0007 to access the subject RFP.

This event will provide critical updates on the CNECTS requirement, featuring a comprehensive walk-through of the draft Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) and Area of Interest (AOI) document(s). Additionally, the Government will host virtual One-on-One meetings exclusively for new small business participants that have not had an opportunity to meet with the CNECTS acquisition team to ensure maximum opportunity for emerging partners to discuss their capabilities for he CNECTS requirements. 2. EVENT DATES & DETAILS Virtual Industry Day: Wednesday, 19 August 2026 Format: Virtual Only (MS Teams) Audience: Open to all interested industry partners. Key Focus: Detailed walk-through and Q&A session regarding the CNECTS draft CSO and AOI. Small Business One-on-One Meetings: Thursday, 20 August 2026 & Friday, 21 August 2026 Format: Virtual Only (MS Teams) Eligibility Requirement (CRITICAL): These sessions are strictly reserved for new small business participants that have not previously met with the CNECTS acquisition team. If your company has already engaged in a One-on-One for this requirement, please do not request a slot for these dates. Space is highly limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis for eligible firms. 3. ONE-ON-ONE REGISTRATION (OPEN NOW) ? Eligible small businesses may begin requesting their 1-on-1 time slots immediately. Space is highly limited and slots will be assigned on a first-come, first-served basis. How to Request: Email the Point of Contact listed below. Required Email Subject Line: CNECTS 1-on-1 Request - [Your Company Name] Information to Include in Request: Company Name & Unique Entity ID (UEI) Primary Point of Contact (Name, Email, Phone) Small Business and/or Socioeconomic Category (e.g., SDVOSB, WOSB, 8(a), HUBZone), if applicable Confirmation Statement: "We confirm that our company has not previously held a One-on-One meeting with the CNECTS acquisition team." 4. NEXT STEPS FOR THE VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY For general attendance at the Virtual Industry Day on August 19 (which does not require a 1-on-1 slot), formal MS Teams dial-in links and draft CSO/AOI materials will be posted here in the coming weeks. No registration is required for the main briefings on August 19. 5. POINTS OF CONTACT Submit your One-on-One meeting requests directly to: Primary POC: Rosalind Davis, Contracting Officer � rosalind.davis.3@spaceforce.mi 14 July 2026 Updated: Important Notice to Industry: Immediate Suspension of CMMC Phase II Requirements On behalf of the SAIO Acquisition Team, we want to ensure all industry partners are aware of a major policy announcement issued today by the Department of War (DoW) Chief Information Officer (CIO) and the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment. Effective immediately, the Department has suspended the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Phase II requirements, which were originally scheduled to go into effect on November 10, 2026. What does this mean? While Phase II is suspended to reduce administrative barriers, the Department maintains a strict cybersecurity posture: Phase I Remains Active: All CMMC Phase I self-assessment requirements remain firmly in place. Contractual Enforcement Continues: Contractual enforcement of cybersecurity remains fully active. All defense contractors must still comply with DFARS 252.204-7012, which requires the implementation of NIST SP 800-171 security controls to protect Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). 9 July 2026 Updated: General Status Updated Regarding the Acquisition Path and Timeline We appreciate your continued interest and your patience as we work through the pre-acquisition phases. This correspondence is to provide a general status update regarding the acquisition path and timeline: Current Review Status: The CNECTS follow-on is a highly complex acquisition that consolidates multiple legacy contracts across critical Space Force installations. At this time, several critical reviews and strategy documents have not yet been approved. Path Forward: Because of the technical and structural complexity of this effort, we are working diligently to secure all necessary senior-level approvals. As soon as we obtain a more definitive pathway and approved strategy, we will provide an updated milestone schedule to Industry. A Viable Requirement: We want to emphasize that this remains a highly viable contract action. The Government is fully committed to this consolidated effort and is actively progressing through the required regulatory steps. Virtual Industry Day: Due to the extensive delay between the initial Industry Day and the upcoming release of the CSO/Area of Interest (AOI), the Space Acquisition and Integration Office (SAIO) plans to host a Virtual-Only Industry Day. The purpose of this event will be to walk through the CSO and the specific AOI requirements prior to their release, aiming to address as many questions as possible before the official solicitation goes live. One-on-One Meetings: In conjunction with these updates, one-on-one (1-1) meetings will be offered to any new requesters that have not previously met with the CNECTS acquisition team. Due to high interest and resource constraints, we are unable to accommodate repeat meetings with previously engaged parties. As a reminder, when the solicitation is released, it will be executed as a 100% Small Business Set-Aside using the Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) phased evaluation process. We encourage you to continue to monitor SAM.gov for all future updates, draft releases, and formal announcements regarding this requirement. Thank you again for your time, interest, and continued support of this mission. 10 June 2026 Updated: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Decision At this time, the acquisition strategy has not been approved. Unfortunately, this process has taken longer than initially anticipated, and the Government is still actively working through the approval process. However, we are able to share an update regarding the SBA's decision: The SBA has officially released the two previous contracts�WICS II and PEDS�from the 8(a) program. Concurrently, the initially approved consolidated Justification and Approval (J&A) decision has been changed. To provide an update on our overall scheduling status: The first 22 eligible small business companies have now been officially scheduled for August 20th and 21st. Calendar invitations with specific times and MS Teams links were sent directly to the designated Point of Contact (POC) today. If your company's request was submitted prior to the official deadline of August 5, 2026, at 9:30 AM MDT, but you were not in the first group of 22, your request is still valid. The CNECTS Program Manager will contact you to schedule your meeting for the overflow sessions occurring the following week (the week of August 24, 2026). If your request was submitted after the deadline, we regret that we are unable to accommodate your firm due to scheduling constraints. We highly encourage your participation in the main Virtual Industry Day on Wednesday, August 19, 2026. Thank you for your inquiry and your continued interest in the CNECTS requirement. We appreciate your patience as we work through the remaining schedule and look forward to your engagement. 13 Aug 2026 Updated: CNECTS Pre-Release Virtual Industry Day Information and More. 1. CNECTS PRE-RELEASE VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY: MS TEAMS DIAL-IN (AUGUST 19, 2026) The CNECTS Pre-Release Virtual Industry Day is open to all interested large and small businesses. No prior registration is required to attend this main session. Date: Wednesday, 19 August 2026 Time: 09:00 AM � 1:00 PM Mountain Standard Time (MST) Location: Virtual Only via Microsoft Teams Join the meeting on your computer, mobile app, or room device: Microsoft Teams meeting (Highlight, Copy & Paste the link below in the browser to access) Join: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993644079118?p=bQaeu9hdFClT0ybufo Meeting ID: 993 644 079 118 Passcode: cR2cH2eb Need help? | System reference Dial in by phone +1 410-874-6740,,963402252# United States, Odenton Find a local number Phone conference ID: 963 402 252# 2. ONE-ON-ONE MEETING INVITATIONS SENT The Government has officially scheduled all calendar invitations for the Small Business One-on-One sessions. These calendar invites were sent today directly to the Point of Contact (POC) identified in your original request. Please check your inbox and spam/junk folders. Your invite contains the specific date, time, and private MS Teams link for your session. Note: If you received a prior email confirming you secured a slot but did not receive a calendar invite today, please contact the Contracting Office immediately. 3. TEAMING & PARTNERSHIP QUESTIONNAIRE The CNECTS effort is a large-scale acquisition, and the Government highly encourages teaming arrangements, joint ventures, and prime/subcontractor partnerships. To facilitate networking among industry partners, we are compiling an "Interested Vendors List" that will be distributed to all participants. If your company wishes to be included on this list to explore partnering opportunities, please complete the short questionnaire by Monday, 24 August 2026 at 12:00 PM MST. (Highlight, Copy & Paste the link below in the browser to access): https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/LkHE57UpWm 05 Aug 2026 Update: CNECTS 1-on-1 Meeting Requests Closed This email is to inform you that the request window for the Small Business One-on-One meetings has officially closed. The final cutoff for submissions was today, August 5, 2026, at 9:30 AM MDT. Due to the late publication of our notice, we are implementing the following scheduling protocols to accommodate our industry partners: For Requests Received PRIOR to the Cutoff (Before 9:30 AM Today): If your request was submitted before the cutoff, your meeting is being accommodated. Due to high demand filling the original August 20th�21st window, your One-on-One meeting will be scheduled for the following week (week of August 24, 2026). The Program Manager will reach out to you shortly to coordinate your specific date and time. For Requests Received AFTER the Cutoff (After 9:30 AM Today): We regret that we cannot accept any further requests. All sessions are fully booked with over 40 requests received. If you secured a slot, you will receive a separate calendar invite shortly with your official appointment details and MS Teams meeting link. Even if you are not participating in a One-on-One session, we highly encourage you to attend the main Pre-Release Virtual Industry Day on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, for a comprehensive walk-through of the forthcoming Commercial Solutions Offering (CSO) and Area of Interest (AOI). Thank you for your time and your interest in supporting the Space Force mission. Respectfully, Rosalind Davis Contracting Officer Space Acquisition and Integration Office (SAIO) 28 July 2026 Update: Correction to Government POC Email Address for One-on-One Requests Primary POC: Rosalind Davis, Contracting Officer � rosalind.davis.3@spaceforce.mil 28 July 2026 Updated: SAVE-THE-DATE: CNECTS Pre-Release Virtual Industry Day & One-on-Ones The Space Acquisition and Integration Office (SAIO), on behalf of the 21st Communications Squadron (21 CS), is pleased to announce a Pre-Release Virtual Industry Day for the CNECTS acquisition. This event will provide critical updates on the CNECTS requirement, featuring a comprehensive walk-through of the draft Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) and Area of Interest (AOI) document(s). Additionally, the Government will host virtual One-on-One meetings exclusively for new small business participants that have not had an opportunity to meet with the CNECTS acquisition team to ensure maximum opportunity for emerging partners to discuss their capabilities for he CNECTS requirements. 2. EVENT DATES & DETAILS Virtual Industry Day: Wednesday, 19 August 2026 Format: Virtual Only (MS Teams) Audience: Open to all interested industry partners. Key Focus: Detailed walk-through and Q&A session regarding the CNECTS draft CSO and AOI. Small Business One-on-One Meetings: Thursday, 20 August 2026 & Friday, 21 August 2026 Format: Virtual Only (MS Teams) Eligibility Requirement (CRITICAL): These sessions are strictly reserved for new small business participants that have not previously met with the CNECTS acquisition team. If your company has already engaged in a One-on-One for this requirement, please do not request a slot for these dates. Space is highly limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis for eligible firms. 3. ONE-ON-ONE REGISTRATION (OPEN NOW) ? Eligible small businesses may begin requesting their 1-on-1 time slots immediately. Space is highly limited and slots will be assigned on a first-come, first-served basis. How to Request: Email the Point of Contact listed below. Required Email Subject Line: CNECTS 1-on-1 Request - [Your Company Name] Information to Include in Request: Company Name & Unique Entity ID (UEI) Primary Point of Contact (Name, Email, Phone) Small Business and/or Socioeconomic Category (e.g., SDVOSB, WOSB, 8(a), HUBZone), if applicable Confirmation Statement: "We confirm that our company has not previously held a One-on-One meeting with the CNECTS acquisition team." 4. title: RFI - Novel or Multifunctional Fibers, Yarns, Coatings/Finishes and Fabrics for Soldier Protection and Comfort (MFFYF)
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army DEVCOM Soldier Center, in coordination with the Product Manager for Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE), to identify potential sources of multifunctional fibers, yarns, fabrics, coatings, or finishes for Soldier protection, thermal comfort and/or physical comfort. The RFI is issued for the purpose of identifying and assessing novel fibers, yarns, fabrics, coatings or finishes. Of primary interest are multifunctional submissions that provide at least two (2) functionalities (e.g., a moisture management fiber knit into a vector protective structure, an oil repellant coating or finish applied to flame resistant fabric). The Government seeks both near- and far-term approaches: Near-Term Solutions (TRL 5�7+): Mature, drop-in, or near-term standalone textile solutions that can be rapidly validated by DEVCOM SC and could be inserted into active military Programs of Record (PORs). Near-term solutions should be able to withstand laundering and abrasion while maintaining functionality. Far-Term Next-Generation Concepts (TRL 2�4): Emerging, exploratory concepts (e.g., novel fiber cross-sections, grooved/star-shaped capillaries, re-entrant geometries, mechanical vector-barrier architectures, vector protective chemistries, biomimetic moisture channels, and advanced microclimate finishes) to inform technology investments for future uniform platforms. title: PACA Special Audits RFQ
description: General The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians, and families. Air Force Services Center supports bases, major commands (MAJCOMs), and the Air Staff by providing technical expertise, launching new initiatives, developing programs and operational procedures, and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures the successful operation of essential food services, fitness and sports centers, childcare and youth programs, lodging accommodations, and recreational opportunities for military members and their families worldwide. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field, and developing new programs supporting installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) centrally manages and administers the Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program, which supports a worldwide mission providing independent oversight of internal controls, cash management, asset protection, and financial management across the enterprise. Background Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families, and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery, operational readiness, and the protection of government interests. Regular independent audits are required to evaluate the financial condition, control environments, and operational efficiencies of Nonappropriated Fund operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations Branch (AFSVC/VFSF) exercises central program oversight to ensure compliance with annual statutory audit requirements under Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 7600.06, Audit of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities and Related Activities, ensuring adequate audit coverage is provided across the enterprise for Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The term "Activities" refers to operational and revenue-generating entities within the Air Force structure. Audit engagements under this Special Audits contract specifically include financial statement audits and performance audits covering: � Accounting practices and transactional compliance; � Internal control environments and segregation of duties; � Cash management, vault operations, and electronic banking; � Fixed asset accountability, tracking, and depreciation; � Inventory valuation, spoilage controls, and physical counts; � Food and beverage operations and food service portfolios; � Centralized shared service center processing; � Venture gaming and electronic slot machine operations; � Supplemental mission dining operations; and � Agreed-upon procedures and special interest compliance reviews. Specific Focus Areas for the PACA Special Audits Program: � A. Shared Service Center (SSC): Conduct performance audits of the Shared Service Center (SSC) at the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) located in San Antonio, TX. The primary objective of the performance audit is to address economy, efficiency, and operational effectiveness. The scope includes core accounting transaction workflows, inter-entity cost allocation methodologies, compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs), operational metrics, and the adequacy of financial management technology system controls. Further details will be outlined in specific delivery order project assignments. � B. Department of the Air Force (DAF) Venture Gaming Program: The DAF Venture Gaming Program operates electronic gaming and slot machine activities at authorized overseas military installations. The program serves as an important nonappropriated revenue generator utilized directly to support and enhance Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs across all Air Force installations. Authorized by DoDI 1015.10 and centrally managed by AFSVC in San Antonio, TX, slot machine operations present unique risks due to regulatory complexities, high cash volumes, and potential for manipulation. Scope includes electronic gaming data systems, meter reconciliations, cash drop and count controls, payout authorizations, jackpot disbursements, internal control safeguards against manipulation or theft, and compliance with federal tax reporting requirements (including IRS Form W-2G processing). � C. Air Force Cadet Dining Fund: The Cadet Dining Fund is a Supplemental Mission Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) operated by the 10th Force Support Squadron (10th FSS) located at the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), Colorado. Supplemental Mission NAFIs receive nonappropriated funds generated from installation mission programs (training, food service, education, security). While congressionally appropriated funds (APF) cover civilian management, custodial services, and facility upkeep, nonappropriated funds are utilized strictly for food purchases and the operational maintenance of cadet meal operations. The fund provides daily dining support for over 4,400 cadets. The Contractor shall perform comprehensive financial statement and operational compliance audits examining food supply procurement, inventory receiving and storage controls, cost-per-meal accounting, meal card verifications, and financial statement accuracy in accordance with USAFAI 34-104 and applicable NAF regulations. � D. Commander�s Special Interest Audits: To address immediate, unplanned operational needs, the Government requires the capacity to execute ad hoc, targeted investigations known as Commander�s Special Interest Audits. These audits may be requested at any given time by Installation Commanders, the AFSVC Commander, or higher headquarters to address immediate operational concerns, suspected material control failures, or strategic risk areas. These ad hoc engagements may encompass any Air Force Installation, NAF Activity, or fund within the scope of this contract, and will be ordered and executed as individual, consolidated performance audit task orders in accordance with the established deliverables and pricing schedules. Scope Air Force Services Center requires the audit services of licensed Certified Public Accountants (CPAs) or CPA firms to perform financial statement audits of Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) financial statements and performance audits of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Services activities, with particular emphasis on high-risk areas identified through preliminary risk assessments and annual selection matrices.

title: Landquart, Gleis- und Perronanlage Phase B, Elektroanlagen
description:
Der Ausbau des Bahnhofs Landquart Phase B ist ein Gemeinschaftsprojekt der RhB und SBB. Es beinhaltet die Modernisierung des gesamten Personenbahnhofs, insbesondere auch für Reisende mit eingeschränkter Mobilität. Herzstück des Projekts bildet der gemeinsame Mittelperron für den komfortablen und zeitsparenden Umstieg zwischen den Zügen der RhB und SBB. Durch den gemeinsamen Perron kann bei beiden Bahnen je ein zusätzliches Gleis mit Perron realisiert werden. Dies bildet den Grundstein für den angestrebten Halbstundentakt. Das Projekt ist in zeitlich vorgelagerte Vorarbeiten und Hauptarbeiten unterteilt. Die Beschaffung für die Niederspannungs- und Telekominstallationen für den Neubau des Dienstgebäude 02 wurden bereits ausgeschrieben und vergeben.

 

Die vorliegende Beschaffung bezieht sich auf die Hauptarbeiten für den Bahnhof gemäss Leistungsverzeichnis.

title: Gullbring Kulturanlegg Tilbygg og ombygging bibliotek
description: Midt-Telemark kommune lyser ut konkurranse på vegne av Gullbring Kulturanlegg AS som er byggherre i dette prosjektet. Gullbring Kulturanlegg ligger i Bø i Midt-Telemark kommune. I dette prosjektet skal det etableres et nytt bibliotek og seremonirom, som delvis innpasses i eksisterende bygg og delvis etableres i et nytt tilbygg over to etasjer, med et samlet areal på cirka 520 m². Eksisterende overbygg over inngangspartiet skal rives. Tilbygget skal oppføres på eksisterende peler fra det tidligere overbygde inngangspartiet samt fire nye peler. Alle pelene er kontrollert og dokumentert av byggherren før totalentreprenøren overtar prosjektet. Prosjektet omfatter ny løfteplattform, ny innvendig trapp og nytt ventilasjonsaggregat. Aggregatet skal betjene både tilbygget og biblioteket sine ombygde lokaler i eksisterende bygg. Eksisterende strøm-, vatn-, brannalarm-, radiator- og sprinkleranlegg skal bygges om og kobles til nye anlegg mens kulturhuset er i drift. Prosjektet omfatter følgende: ● Etablering av nytt bibliotek og seremonirom i Gullbring Kulturanlegg. ● Tilbygg over to etasjer på eksisterende peler og fire nye peler. Alle peler er kontrollert og dokumentert av byggherren før oppstart. ● Riving av eksisterende overbygg over inngangspartiet. ● Ny løfteplattform, ny innvendig trapp og nytt ventilasjonsaggregat. ● Ombygging og tilkobling av eksisterende infrastruktur som f.eks. strøm, vann, alarmanlegg og sprinkler mm. ● Ny inngang og ny midlertidig publikumstilkomst/beredskapsvei. ● Prosjektering for alle fag. Arbeidene blir gjennomført mens kulturhuset er i full drift. Det medfører krav til fysisk skille, kontrollert adgang og koordinering mot drift og publikum.

description: This EU tender aims to provide consulting and system integration services for the further development of the Elia Digital Platform (EDP). description: In the injection and extraction sections of the SIS100, beam dynamics requirements necessitate vacuum chamber and component apertures of up to approximately 320 mm to contain both the orbit beam and the injected or extracted ion beams. title: Sweden – Evaluation consultancy services – Metod och processtöd - platsutveckling
description: UPPDRAGET OCH DESS OMFATTNING Västerbottens regionala utvecklingsstrategi 2020–2030 slår fast att länets utveckling förutsätter fördjupade och gränsöverskridande samarbeten. Visionen är en attraktiv region där olikheter skapar utvecklingskraft. Flera förhållanden begränsar i dag den förmågan: • Arbete organiseras i stuprör, vilket försvårar samverkan mellan lokal, regional, nationell och internationell nivå. • Små och medelstora företag behandlas ofta som en homogen grupp trots att deras behov skiljer sig åt. • Kunskap, relationer och nätverk är i hög grad personberoende och riskerar att gå förlorade när projekt avslutas eller nyckelpersoner slutar. • Lokala initiativ synliggörs inte alltid på regional nivå, vilket minskar möjligheten att ta tillvara erfarenheter och resultat. • Kommunerna har en central roll i den regionala utvecklingen men saknar ofta resurser, kapacitet och tidig delaktighet. • Finansierings- och styrsystem är ofta för tröga för att stödja missionsdriven omställning. • Resultat och metoder från internationella samarbeten, särskilt inom Interreg, integreras inte tillräckligt i de regionala utvecklingsprocesserna. Det finns därmed behov av stärkt förmåga till samverkan och samhandling mellan aktörer, och av strukturer som kopplar samman behov, kunskap och resurser mellan nivåer. Det handlar om funktioner som ger överblick över pågående initiativ, synliggör kopplingar mellan aktörer och möjliggör mer differentierade former av stöd till företag och organisationer. Det handlar också om former för tidig delaktighet, tydligare rollfördelning och ökad förmåga att omsätta resultat från projektverksamheten i konkret regional utveckling, policyutveckling och innovationsprocesser. En stärkt koppling mellan aktörer och nivåer ger bättre förutsättningar att ta tillvara befintlig kunskap, identifiera kompletterande insatser och minska dubbelarbete. Erfarenheter från europeiska samarbeten kan i högre grad integreras i regionala utvecklingsprocesser. Lokala behov kan tydligare relateras till regionala, nationella och europeiska prioriteringar, vilket ökar precisionen i insatser riktade till företag och organisationer. Denna upphandling avser metod- och processtöd för platsutveckling. Uppdraget har platsen som utvecklingsobjekt: att analysera en plats förutsättningar, samla dess aktörer kring en gemensam riktning och leda arbetet från dialog till konkreta insatser.

description: The Virginia Contracting Activity (VACA) intends to execute a contract modification to increase the ceiling for the Solutions for Intelligence Analysis (SIA) 3 Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) (including the following IDIQs: HHM402-19-D-0005, HHM402-19-D-0007, HHM402-19-D-0008, HHM402-19-D-0009, HHM402-19-D-0010, HHM402-19-D-0012, HHM402-19-D-0013, HHM402-19-D-0014, HHM402-19-D-0015, HHM402-19-D-0016, HHM402-19-D-0017, HHM402-19-D-0018, HHM402-19-D-0019, HHM402-19-D-0020, HHM402-19-D-0021, and HHM402-19-D-0022) pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, only with limited responsible sources and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The current SIA 3 IDIQ is a multi-award, IDIQ type contract in which the contractor shall provide a broad range of intelligence analytical, scientific, engineering, analytic enabling, and counterintelligence/human intelligence services in support of the Defense Intelligence Enterprise and associated stakeholder organizations. The proposed ceiling increase is from $17.1 billion by $12.9 billion to $30 billion in total. This increase allows for continued mission essential work to be performed by the awarded firms and the soon-to-be awarded On-Ramp of small businesses through the last day of the contract on August 4, 2029. The Agency anticipates recompeting SIA 3, starting in 2027 to have a new contract awarded prior to the August 2029 end of the ordering period. Please see https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/827c31242c0a458c9d4e732df28bd129/view for SIA 4�s special notice. The proposed contract action is for supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with the multiple awardees of SIA 3 and the anticipated On-Ramp awardees of SIA 3. Interested parties may identify their interest and comparable solution to the requirement. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit within fifteen (15) days of this publication a comparable solution for government consideration. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based on the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The NAICS for this requirement is 541990. Interested parties may provide their comparable solution to meet this requirement no later than fifteen (15) days after the publication of this notice via email to Raqeeba Mohammed at Raqeeba.Mohammed@dodiis.mil and Christopher Nietubyc at Christopher.Nietubyc@dodiis.mil. Additionally, any response to this notice must show clear, compelling and convincing evidence that the comparable solution will be advantageous to the Government. A determination not to modify the contract based on the responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. The intent of this notice is for informational purposes only. No reimbursement for any costs connected with providing comparable solutions will be provided.

title: Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Europese aanbesteding voor een gecertificeerde Microsoft Dynamics inrichting- en supportpartner
description: Talland College heeft sinds de zomer van 2024 Microsoft Dynamics 365 in gebruik als CRM-systeem. De initiële inrichting en toepassing van het CRM-systeem is gerealiseerd binnen het team Marketing & Communicatie. Binnen de organisatie bestaat de wens om Microsoft Dynamics 365 organisatiebreed in te zetten. Odabrani ponuditelj dužan je svakodnevno obići sve lokacije fontana u svrhu utvrđivanja njihove funkcionalnosti. Dužan je napraviti i dostaviti Naručitelju u pisanom obliku tjedni plan čišćenja i održavanja fontana prema kojem će obavljati ugovornu uslugu. Rezervni dijelovi koji se ugrađuju moraju biti novi, nabavljeni od proizvođača ili ovlaštenog dobavljača, provjerene kvalitete dokazane uvjerenjem/izjavom o sukladnosti proizvoda-za uvoznu opremu. Od Odabranog ponuditelja, Naručitelj za uslugu popravka traži jamstvo u trajanju od najmanje 12 (dvanaest) mjeseci, a za ugrađene dijelove i opremu dužina jamstva ovisi o jamstvu proizvođača čiju je presliku potrebno priložiti kod obračuna Odabrani ponuditelj obvezan je tijekom trajanja ugovora postojeće instalacije, uređaje i opremu fontana kontinuirano održavati u stanju tehničke ispravnosti. Prilikom svakodnevnog obilaska osoba ovlaštena od strane Odabranog ponuditelja dužna je voditi dnevnik o provedenoj kontroli tehničke ispravnosti instalacija, uređaja i opreme, temeljem čega se sačinjava izvješće o kvarovima. Ukoliko Odabrani ponuditelj tijekom svakodnevnog obilaska utvrdi kvar na instalacijama, uređajima i bazenskoj opremi, obvezan je o tome bez odgađanja izvijestiti Naručitelja putem e-maila. Ukoliko Odabrani ponuditelj tijekom pružanja usluge utvrdi da su se pojavile okolnosti koje ugrožavaju život i zdravlje ljudi ili susjedne objekte, dužan je zastati s radom te o tome odmah izvijestiti Naručitelja. Odabrani ponuditelj obvezan je tijekom trajanja ugovora osigurati jedan tim na raspolaganju 24 sata dnevno (radnim danom, vikendom i blagdanom), za izlazak na poziv hitne službe ili Naručitelja u slučaju izvanredne situacije kao što je poplavljenje uslijed puknuća instalacije ili požar na instalacijama, kako bi pristupio lokaciji i isključio fontanu iz rada i zatvorio dotok vode. Popravak i otklon štete odrađuje se prvi radni dan. Odabrani ponuditelj dužan je sastaviti i voditi dokumentaciju o svim fontanama sa popisom i specifikacijom opreme, njihovom izmjenom i dopunom kod popravaka. Kod isteka Ugovora, dokumentaciju je dužan predati Naručitelju kao sastavni dio Završnog izvješća o stanja fontana. Ukoliko Odbrani ponuditelj ne dostavi Završno izvješće i traženu dokumentaciju, Naručitelj ima pravo angažirati neovisnu stručnu osobu za izradu dokumentacije, popisa i specifikacije opreme, funkcionalnog stanja fontana. Troškovi izrade dokumentacije podmirit će se iz jamstva za uredno ispunjenje ugovora na temelju okvirnog sporazuma. Izvršitelj se obvezuje voditi evidenciju o količini pružene usluge te uz svaki mjesečni račun priložiti mjesečni izvještaj o izvršenju Ugovora s pratećom fotodokumentacijom stanja prije i poslije izvršene usluge, kao i specifikaciju izvršene usluge.

Un même candidat ne peut être titulaire attributaire de plus d'un lot par corps d'état. Le candidat indique dans sa lettre de candidature (ou DC1) son ordre de préférence entre les deux lots d'un même corps d'état. Si un candidat obtient l'offre économiquement la plus avantageuse sur ces deux lots, il sera attributaire du lot qu'il a placé en première position; l'autre lot est attribué au candidat classé deuxième. À défaut d'ordre de préférence, il est attributaire du lot pour lequel l'écart de note avec le candidat classé deuxième est le plus élevé. Cette limitation s'applique également aux groupements et aux sociétés liées au sens des articles L233-1 et L233-3 du code de commerce. Si le nombre de candidatures recevables ou d'offres régulières, acceptables et appropriées est inférieur à deux pour un lot, le candidat ayant présenté l'offre économiquement la plus avantageuse aux deux lots d'un même corps d'état se verra attribuer ces derniers

title: United States Space Force Integration Facility
description: USACE Louisville District issues this Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to identify and select the single most highly qualified Design-Build Team to execute the United States Space Force (USSF) Integration Facility (UIF) project at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio.The project provides a new, multi-floor, approximately 333,700-square-foot secure USSF Integration Facility and a physical connection to active Building F/10854. The Design-Builder must plan and execute all work to avoid unscheduled interruption of 24/7 mission operations, utilities, communications, and existing secure-facility accreditation.

The Government is considering alternative space if economically advantageous. In making this determination, the Government will consider, among other things, the availability of alternative space that potentially can satisfy the Government�s requirements, as well as costs likely to be incurred through relocating, such as physical move costs, replication of tenant improvements and telecommunication infrastructure, non-productive agency downtime, and costs, including rent, related to vacating the current location prior to lease termination. The Government�s desire is for a full-service lease to include base rent, CAM, utilities, and janitorial services for a retail space for an Armed Forces Career Center for a term of five (5) years with Government termination rights and location within the delineated area specified above. Non-exclusive parking for government vehicles must be provided 24 hours 7 days. Offered space must meet Government requirements per the terms of the Government Lease. Interested respondents may include building owners and representatives with the exclusive right to represent buildings owners. Representatives of building owners must include the exclusivity granting the exclusive right to represent the building owner with their response to this advertisement. Space shall be located in a professional retail setting and preferably not within close proximity to residential areas, railroad tracks, or power transmission lines. Space should not be located within the 100-year flood plain or wetland unless the Government has determined it to be the only practicable alternative. Space should not be located near establishments whose primary operation is the sale of alcoholic beverages, firearms sold/discharged, marijuana dispensaries, or where there are tenants or invitees related to drug treatment or detention facilities. Employee and visitor entrances of the Building must be connected to public sidewalks or street by continuous, accessible sidewalks. Regularly scheduled public transportation (if provided by municipality) during the workday is required within 1,000 feet. The parking-to-square -foot ratio available onsite shall at least meet current local code requirements. Restricted or metered parking of one hour or less within the four-block area of the space does not meet parking requirements. Subleases are not acceptable. Retail space should be on the ground floor. Space configuration shall be conducive to an efficient layout. Considerations for an efficient layout include, but are not limited to, the following: size and location of interior fire (support) walls, size and number of columns, column placement, bay depts, window size and placement, convector size and placement, electrical and telephone accessibility, and angles, curves, or offsets that will result in an inefficient use of space. The following space configurations will not be considered: Space with atriums and other areas interrupting contiguous space, extremely long or narrow runs of space (more than twice as long as wide), irregularly shaped space configurations or other unusual building features adversely affective usage. Columns cannot exceed two (2�) square feet and space between columns and/or walls cannot be less than twenty (20�) feet. The offered space must meet or be capable of meeting Government requirements for Security, Fire Life Safety and Handicapped Accessibility. If space offered is above ground level, there must be elevator access. The Government requires a fully serviced lease. All services, janitorial supplies, utilities, and tenant alterations are to be provided as part of the rental consideration. title: Anskaffelse av elektrisk kraft
description: ØFAS skal inngå en treårig avtale om kjøp av elektrisk kraft til anleggene som angitt i konkurransegrunnlaget. Leverandør skal handle i det fysiske kraftmarkedet på vegne av oppdragsgiver. Fastpris gjelder for faktisk forbruk opp til en fast månedsgrense på 70 % av historisk gjennomsnittsforbruk for kalendermåneden. Resten av forbruket kjøpes til spotpris med avtalt påslag. Det er ingen plikt for ØFAS til å kjøpe et minstevolum.

title: Møbel til nye Trudvang skule
description: Bakgrunn og formål Ny barneskule og SFO blir dimensjonert for 700 elevar og om lag 70 tilsette pluss fasilitetar for drift og reinhald. Elevane er fordelt på 17 klassar i trinn 1-4 og 13 klassar i trinn 5-7. Prosjektet er delt i to byggetrinn. Byggetrinn 1 er planlagt til å vere ferdig 01. juli 2027 og inkluderer trinnareal til 1-4. trinn, SFO, kjøkken, bibliotek og administrasjonsareal med kontorfløy og pauseareal.. Byggetrinn 2 er planlagt til å vere ferdig desember 2028 og inkluderer trinnareal 5.-7. trinn, samt fleksavdeling, spesialrom, fellesareal og idrett. Byggetrinn 1 er indikert med gul farge på vedlagte teikningar. Det er tenkt gjenbruk av eksisterande møbel i så stor grad som hensiktsmessig. Men det er også behov for nye møbel, særleg møbel som understøtter den pedagogiske visjonen til skulen. Denne anskaffinga gjeld behov for møbel til byggetrinn 1. Anskaffinga inkluderer også opsjon på møbel til byggetrinn 2. Visjonen Visjonen for det nye skulebygg i Sogndal kan godt illustrerast med eit sitat frå samskapingsmøte om nytt skulebygg. "Ingen må gå aleine", elev 2. klasse Det nye skuleanlegget i Sogndal sentrum er ei stor investering i born og unge sitt oppvekstmiljø. Gjennom dei neste 60 åra skal born som veks opp i Sogndal starte skulegangen sin på denne skulen. På skulen skal borna få opne opp dører mot verda og framtida, dei tilsette skal ha ein arbeidsplass som legg til rette for å kunne bidra til borna si utforskartrong. Skuleområdet skal vere eit nærområde som blir nytta til leik og sosiale aktivitetar, også utanfor skuletida. Inventaret skal understøtte dei pedagogiske ambisjonane i prosjektet, visjonen for den nye skulen og intensjonane i læreplanane. Samstundes skal anskaffinga ha høg miljøambisjon og omfatte vurdering og gjenbruk av eksisterande møblar og inventar der det er pedagogisk, funksjonelt og økonomisk forsvarleg.
